key_insight: AI can speed up electrical machine design by acting as a physics-aware surrogate and optimization aid, but it must remain grounded in simulation and experimental validation.
engineering_relevance: The work is relevant to designing high-performance machines that satisfy power density, thermal, mechanical, acoustic, manufacturability, cost, and sustainability constraints.
method: Surrogate modeling and machine learning to approximate FEM-based performance.
Physics-informed and Bayesian methods for uncertainty-aware prediction and optimization.
Active learning and emerging generative approaches for inverse and multi-objective design.
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes workflow-level evidence from simulation-driven and AI-assisted design studies, while noting that reported validation is often limited and data are frequently generated by FEM.
watch_item: A key concern is weak extrapolation beyond training topologies and insufficient reporting of uncertainty, manufacturability, and experimental verification.
paper_title: AI-Driven Electrical Machine Design: From Surrogate-Assisted Optimization to Trustworthy, Manufacturable, and Sustainable Design Workflows
